sources.title: Assessment of Safety of a Fully Implanted Endovascular Brain-Computer Interface for Severe Paralysis in 4 Patients: The Stentrode With Thought-Controlled Digital Switch (SWITCH) Study
sources.observed_result: A first-in-human prospective study implanted an endovascular electrode system connected to a subcutaneous receiver-transmitter; four participants completed 12-month follow-up, maintained signal, and controlled a computer, with the article reporting no device-related serious adverse event causing death or permanent increased disability.

sources.title: Minimally invasive implantation of scalable high-density cortical microelectrode arrays for multimodal neural decoding and stimulation
sources.observed_result: Thin-film cortical arrays inserted through a cranial micro-slit supported high-channel-count neural recording, decoding, and focal stimulation across animal experiments and human pilot procedures; individual electrodes could be configured for recording or stimulation.

sources.title: Effects of transcranial magnetic stimulation on the human brain recorded with intracranial electrocorticography
sources.observed_result: TMS delivered to dorsolateral prefrontal cortex in neurosurgical participants produced local and connected downstream intracranial evoked potentials measured with ECoG, providing direct human evidence that non-invasive stimulation can produce target- and network-dependent measurable effects.

sources.title: Efficacy of kinesthetic motor imagery based brain computer interface combined with tDCS on upper limb function in subacute stroke
sources.observed_result: A human rehabilitation study evaluated a motor-imagery BCI combined with transcranial direct-current stimulation, providing evidence for a non-invasive BCI-plus-electrical-stimulation interaction rather than direct semantic neural writing.

sources.title: A multiple session dataset of NIRS recordings from stroke patients controlling brain-computer interface
sources.observed_result: The published dataset contains more than 50 hours of NIRS recordings from 15 stroke patients across 237 motor-imagery BCI sessions, including online performance and longitudinal multi-session data.
